defects.evidence: Turn 4: 'Why did the operator believe adjustment was necessary?' framed explicitly; Turn 2 surfaced equipment drift as the latent cause; Turn 4 AI-suggested hypothesis confirmed both equipment drift and SOP ambiguity as interdependent root causes, explicitly superseding 'operator error' label

Turn 6: 'Are there any CAPAs addressing the equipment recalibration or the SOP/change-control defect — or is retraining OP-2847 the only action on record?' — explicitly flagged retraining-only CAPA as incomplete against systemic root causes
Turn 7: 'Was any effectiveness check defined for any action?' and Turn 6 defendant confirmed 'effectiveness_check: null' with no follow-up compression runs monitored

Turn 3: 'Were any other lots compressed on RP-04 since the last calibration reviewed for weight-variation trends?' — explicitly probed scope expansion to other lots/operators; Turn 8 further probed whether Rev 4 gap was flagged to all operators

Turn 4: SOP revision history and training records gap surfaced; Turn 5 confirmed CC-2023-1847 had no risk assessment; defendant confirmed operator trained on Rev 3 with read-and-sign only on Rev 4 — training record gap explicitly resolved

Turn 2: Grill immediately probed WO-2024-0156 and hopper drift, surfacing the supervisor's 'hopper jamming' statement as equipment-backed; the conflicting statements were resolved by reference to maintenance evidence rather than left unresolved

false_gaps.description: Grill flagged 'cause smuggled into problem statement' as Branch 1 and spent a full turn on it
false_gaps.why_spurious: While technically a documentation quality issue, this is a minor stylistic point not in the planted defects and consumed a full turn that could have gone to substantive gaps; however it did not mislead the investigation

root_cause_rationale: Grill drove past 'operator did not follow SOP' to two interdependent systemic causes: (a) unrecalibrated equipment drift documented 18 months prior and confirmed 2 weeks before the deviation, and (b) SOP Rev 4 removing a compensating control without risk assessment or hands-on retraining. Explicitly invoked Reason's Swiss-cheese model (Turn 3) and Rasmussen's SRK framework (Turn 5), satisfying the highest depth criterion.
capa_rationale: +1: Turn 6 explicitly checked that CAPA-2024-0847-001 addresses none of the three systemic root causes (equipment drift, SOP gap, change control failure). +1: Turn 6 demanded preventive actions for equipment recalibration, SOP revision, and CC-2023-1847 risk assessment — explicitly rejected retraining-only as incomplete. +1: Turn 7 demanded a measurable effectiveness check and flagged null effectiveness_check as a red flag, asking whether monitored compression runs or audits were planned.

leading_examples.why: Grill stated 'AI-suggested, to confirm: the true root cause is (a) equipment drift left unrecalibrated despite two recommendations, and/or (b) an SOP with no procedure for an operator who observes weight variation mid-run' — this fed both candidate root causes directly to the defendant rather than asking open-ended why questions, partially anchoring the answer. Labeled as AI-suggested which mitigates but does not eliminate the leading effect.

termination_rationale: Grill closed all seven branches explicitly, converting unanswerable points (batch records, equipment status post-deviation, QA closure rationale, production schedule) into tracked open items with named owners and evidence requirements. Final summary table provided. No looping or redundant re-asking observed.
overall_comment: Exemplary grill: surfaced all 6 planted defects, drove to systemic root cause with appropriate theoretical lenses, demanded preventive CAPA and measurable effectiveness checks, and cleanly converted evidence gaps into tracked open items — with only one minor leading question that was partially mitigated by explicit AI-suggestion labeling.
